title: job_watch.go is a 6,564-line eight-concern file
note: Verified: 6564 lines, 291 funcs, 259 commits (11 in 30d). Session methods at job_watch.go:5709-6170 (drainPendingWatchSends, driveChildrenWithUndeliveredAttention 5753, childStopGated 5944, ...) operate on child sessions; session_jobtree_drain.go (1750 lines) and subagents.go:1546 driveSubagentNotificationTurn already own sibling logic. docs/architecture.md:330,389,423 and the S12 row of docs/product/subsystems.md:155 name job_watch.go as home.

title: fire-a-watch funnel hand-copied across six sites
note: Overstated. Only three sites share the breaker funnel (noteConditionFireLocked): onSessionEvent 3298, feedJobOutputWithProvenance 3602, fireAttachScan 3714/3728 (twice, separate lock pairs, confirmed). runTerminalCatchup (3761) never touches the breaker, fireProgressTick (4167) explicitly says periodic ticks never trip the budget, and completeExpired is a teardown. The claimed drift (feedJobOutput breaks on budget crossing, onSessionEvent cannot) is not drift: onSessionEvent fires at most once per watch per event, so there is no match loop to break. There IS a real ordering difference: onSessionEvent records sends, then clears over-budget watches, then enqueues (teardown notification rides with the event's batch); feedJobOutput enqueues, records sends, then clears. A shared flush must preserve both orders or the first-wake semantics change. Realistic saving is ~-60, not -150.
revised_fix_plan: Extract only the shared pieces for the three condition-fire sites: a helper that does noteConditionFireLocked + send-vs-notify build + countWatchDelivery under jm.mu, and keep each site's post-unlock ordering explicit (or parameterize it). Leave fireProgressTick, runTerminalCatchup and expire paths alone. Characterization tests for budget crossing mid-chunk and for the onSessionEvent notification order before touching.

title: Watch teardown transaction open-coded in many places
note: Core confirmed: clearWatch (job_watch.go:1639-1682), autoClearWatchOverBudgetNotification (2018-2037) and abandonRunningJobs (jobs.go:913-950) all do mark rejecting -> unlock -> appendWatchTeardownBatch/appendAbandonSnapshots -> rollback or detach+removeWatchSendTerminalSnapshots+forget. Helper counts roughly match (removeWatchSendTerminalSnapshots 16 prod refs, forgetDetached 7, markWatchConfigSnapshotsRejectingLocked 6, rollbackWatchConfigsRejecting 5). But sites differ materially (clear returns the error; abandon swallows it into a notification; budget path also resets budgetTripped under the same critical section), so a single watchTeardown value must model three failure policies. rollbackWatchBudgetTeardown/Locked is a normal lock/Locked pair (3+2 refs), not slop worth its own item. abandonRunningJob (jobs.go:953) is genuinely dead (0 prod callers, //nolint:unused) and near-duplicates abandonRunningJobs. Severity high overstated; risk is medium-high and the saving is closer to -100.
revised_fix_plan: Stage it: (1) delete dead abandonRunningJob (finding 7). (2) Add only red-first persist-failure tests for clearWatch, auto-clear and abandon asserting watch live again with delivery re-enabled. (3) Then extract a begin/rollback/commit helper used by those three sites, one per commit. Do not collapse the three failure policies.

title: configureWatchWithHooks is a 217-line function
note: Confirmed: function spans job_watch.go:764-980; only prod caller is configureWatch (761) passing watchConfigureHooks{}; hooks used by job_watch_core_config_fuzz_test.go:229,250. validateWatchSendTarget (1249) is a pass-through to validateWatchSendDeliveryTarget(target, _ watchArgs) with an unused param. Send-target trimming split in two ifs (778-787), guard repeated at 679 and 822. MISSED by the audit: job_watch_timer_identity_test.go:214-263 is an AST guard looking up the function by name 'configureWatchWithHooks' and counting calls inside its body; splitting or renaming it requires rewriting that guard in the same change. Also the hooks race tests (beforeTargetRevalidate/afterDetachedTeardown) have no real-sync alternative cheaply, so 'drive the race with real sync' is unlikely.
revised_fix_plan: Delete validateWatchSendTarget wrapper and unused param first (tiny, safe). Collapse the two send-target trim ifs. Then split out installWatch, updating job_watch_timer_identity_test.go's AST guard to follow. Keep hooks parameter as is.

No evenerfuzz-tagged non-test file in agent/ references them (only agent/sandbox has tagged non-test files), so moving them to tagged _test.go files is the right home. title: Receiver/visibility matching duplicated; list and inspect disagree
note: Duplication is real: watchConfigMatchesReceiver/watchHistoryMatchesReceiver vs the inline matches closure in watchListToolResultForReceiverShapes (2573-2587), plus separate key-based matchers at 5528-5583. But the headline 'list and inspect disagree' is not supported: inspectReceiverWatchByIDShapes (2672) checks delegate shape then session shape, which for a unique watch id returns the same row the list pass would. The one real asymmetry is clearStableReceiverWatchByID (session_tools_jobs.go:374-383), which uses non-Shapes inspect and a delegate-keyed clear, while inspect at line 249 uses Shapes; whether that is intentional (clear only for stable receiver watches) was not confirmed. Also watchListToolResultForReceiver (the non-Shapes twin) is test-only (finding 7).
revised_fix_plan: Delete the dead non-Shapes list twin (finding 7), then dedupe the matcher closure. Separately ask whether session-keyed descendant watches should be clearable through job_watch clear; if so that is a behavior change needing TDD, not part of this refactor.

title: Send-rail delivery state across ten maps/sets

title: Lane-disposal tunables and override stack in jobs.go
note: Misplacement confirmed: laneClosePassBudget/laneTailWarnThreshold used only by session_worktree_close.go; laneSweepDelay/laneGrace by session_worktree_sweep.go/relock/session_init/session_tools_worktree.go (jobs.go:224-289). But the override stack is not mere over-building: SetLaneClosePassBudget's doc says it exists so end-to-end tests shorten the budget 'without racing a close already running in the background'. A plain package var assigned by tests would be a data race under -race, and TestSetLaneClosePassBudgetRestoresOutOfOrder (session_worktree_close_test.go:70) pins out-of-order restore. Replacing it is unsafe as proposed.
revised_fix_plan: Move the block (constants, vars, laneClosePassBudget, SetLaneClosePassBudget) to session_worktree_close.go with no logic change. Do not replace the override stack.
